questions.q: What specific problem does a failover group solve that plain geo-replication does not?
options: It replicates data faster
It manages a stable listener endpoint so the application never needs to know which region is currently primary, instead of requiring every client to be told by hand to reconnect after a failover
It eliminates the need for a secondary server
It encrypts data during replication
questions.explain: Geo-replication alone replicates data but leaves the connection-endpoint problem unsolved — the failover group adds exactly that missing piece.

questions.q: Which cmdlet actually creates Overlook's failover group resource?
options: CREATE FAILOVER GROUP (T-SQL)
New-AzSqlDatabaseFailoverGroup
Add-AzSqlDatabaseToFailoverGroup
New-AzSqlDatabase
questions.explain: A failover group is a server-level Azure resource with no T-SQL equivalent — it's created via PowerShell's New-AzSqlDatabaseFailoverGroup, the Azure CLI, or the Portal.

questions.q: What does `-GracePeriodWithDataLossHours 1` on the failover group actually control?
options: How long backups are retained
How long the automatic failover policy waits before triggering, to avoid reacting to a brief, transient outage
How often geo-replication syncs data
The TDE encryption key rotation interval
questions.explain: The grace period is a deliberate trade-off between a faster RTO and avoiding an unnecessary failover triggered by a false alarm.

questions.q: After the failover group is set up, what does Overlook's scheduling application connect to?
options: The individual primary server's name, updated manually after each failover
A stable listener endpoint DNS name (overlook-fg.database.windows.net) that Azure automatically points at whichever server is currently primary
Both servers simultaneously, chosen at random
The secondary server's name only
questions.explain: The entire point of the failover group is that the application never needs to know or care which physical region is currently primary.

options: Manual-only failover triggered by a DBA
The group monitoring the primary's health and failing over on its own if it detects an outage, without anyone having to notice and trigger it manually
Automatic deletion of the secondary database
Automatic backup scheduling
questions.explain: Automatic failover removes the dependency on a human noticing the outage and triggering the failover by hand.
